Eggs of Cloeon dipterum measure approximately 0.0167 cm  in length, a dimension typical for the family Baetidae. Upon hatching, the newly emerged prolarva, still enclosed in the embryonic cuticle, has a body length of about 0.0554 cm [Lb = about 0.0554 cm], and the dry weight at birth is a mere 0.0009 mg . The first free-living larval instar emerges after an egg incubation period that, at a constant water temperature of 20 °C [T = 20 °C], lasts approximately 10 days [ab = approximately 10 days]. At 20 °C [T = 20 °C], the initial dry weight of a freshly hatched individual is estimated at 0.0006 mg , a value extrapolated from data on the confamilial Ecdyonurus dispar. From this modest beginning, the first instar larva attains a body length of 0.1962 cm  and a dry mass of 0.02078 mg . The head capsule, a sclerotized structure that grows in discrete increments, measures 0.0330 cm  in width at this stage, reflecting the rigid exoskeletal constraints of instar-specific growth.

At 20 °C [T = 20 °C], as the actively growing larva passes through successive moults, its morphological parameters increase in a stepwise fashion. During the second instar, the body length reaches 0.2630 cm  while the dry weight rises to 0.06111 mg  and the head capsule width expands to 0.0422 cm . By the third instar, these values shift to a body length of 0.3654 cm , a dry weight of 0.11754 mg , and a head width of 0.0584 cm . The fourth instar continues this trajectory with a body length of 0.4988 cm , a dry mass of 0.32165 mg , and a head capsule measuring 0.0732 cm . This pattern of exponential biomass accumulation is characteristic of ephemeropteran larval development, where each successive stadium allows for greater ingestion of detritus and algal material from the benthic substrate.

At 20 °C [T = 20 °C], the fifth instar represents a notable phase of accelerated growth. Individuals at this stage display a body length of 0.6015 cm , a dry weight of 0.85538 mg , and a head width of 0.0992 cm , with the duration of this instar spanning 4.6 days  at a temperature of 20 °C [T = 20 °C]. The food uptake during this stadium is measured at 0.00001683 grams . During the sixth instar, the body length reaches 0.6845 cm , the dry weight climbs to 1.09150 mg , and the head capsule enlarges to 0.1092 cm . This stage, lasting 5.3 days  at the same temperature, is marked by a significantly higher ingestion rate, with a food uptake of 0.00004175 grams . For females, the body length at the completion of this sixth instar is recorded as 0.6845 cm [Lp = 0.6845 cm].

The final larval instars are characterised by a plateau in body size and a reduction in feeding activity. In the seventh instar, the body length is 0.6703 cm , the dry weight peaks at 1.10490 mg , and the head width is 0.1153 cm ; this stage persists for 3 days  at 20 °C [T = 20 °C] and is associated with a food uptake of 0.00002577 grams . During the eighth instar, the body length remains stable at 0.6745 cm , while the dry weight declines slightly to 1.02448 mg  and the head capsule of the nymphal form measures 0.1092 cm . The instar duration is brief at 2.3 days  at 20 °C [T = 20 °C], and ingestion drops to 0.00001485 grams . In the ninth and final nymphal stage, the body length is 0.6695 cm , the dry weight falls to 0.91994 mg , and the head capsule again measures 0.1153 cm . This last instar lasts only 1.1 days  at 20 °C [T = 20 °C], with a minimal food uptake of only 0.00000045 grams , reflecting the cessation of feeding prior to the final moult to the subimago.

The transition to the winged adult form is demarcated by the emergence of the subimago, which for males occurs at 30 days since birth  at 20 °C [T = 20 °C], whereas a second, slower developmental pathway yields an emergence time of 144.02 days since birth  at the same temperature — a variation that may reflect differences in larval resource acquisition or sex-linked developmental constraints. Attainment of sexual maturity, or puberty, is reached at 23.6 days since birth [tp = 23.6 days since birth] at 20 °C [T = 20 °C], though an alternative record places this milestone at 111.56 days since birth [tp = 111.56 days since birth] under identical thermal conditions. The duration from the onset of puberty to the moment of emergence is a brief 6.4 days from the onset of puberty [tp = 6.4 days from the onset of puberty] at 20 °C [T = 20 °C]. At emergence, male subimagoes exhibit a body length of 0.82 cm  and a wet weight of 8.2 mg , while females are slightly larger, with a body length of 0.92 cm  and a wet mass of 13.6 mg  — a pattern of sexual dimorphism consistent with the greater reproductive investment required of female ephemeropterans. The wing length of the female imago is 1.03 cm . Following the final moult to the imago, the adult lifespan is short, lasting 21 days [am = 21 days] at 20 °C [T = 20 °C], during which feeding does not occur, meaning that all energetic resources are directed toward mate location and reproduction. Fecundity is strongly mediated by larval nutrition: at 20 °C [T = 20 °C], females reared under a high food treatment produced an average of 463.889 eggs [N_R_i = 463.889 eggs] , those on a medium diet yielded 319.444 eggs [N_R_i = 319.444 eggs] , and those on a low food ration produced only 216.667 eggs [N_R_i = 216.667 eggs] .
